newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmiri Moslems, Hindus in standoff over rights.
newsitem.headline: Kashmiri Moslems, Hindus in standoff over rights.

text.p: Moslem separatists from Kashmir and exiled Hindus confronted each other in an angry standoff in the Indian capital on Tuesday, claiming they had been the victims of human rights violations.
"We want freedom," Moslem separatists from the All Parties Hurriyat Conference shouted during a protest coinciding with world human rights day.
Some 1,000 separatist demonstrators, most of them women who had come in a convoy of buses from the Kashmir valley, marched across part of New Delhi to the United Nations office.
"Stop molesting Kashmiri women," several placards, carried by Moslem women and children, read.
The separatists were met by about 50 Hindus who fled Kashmir after a separatist insurgency erupted in 1990.
"Go back killers," "Leave Kashmir," the Hindu exiles, called Pandits, shouted.
Police manning barricades dividing the two rival camps restrained irate Pandits from skirmishing with the separatists. There were no reports of injuries.

More than 20,000 people have been killed in the seven-year revolt in Kashmir. Dozens of militant groups opposed to Indian rule in the Himalayan region are fighting for either independence or merger with Pakistan.
India accuses Pakistan of arming and training guerrillas, but Islamabad denies the charge.

Several hundred thousand Hindus left the Kashmir valley after the militancy broke out. Many of them live in spartan refugee camps in Jammu, the winter capital of Jammu and Kashmir state, and around New Delhi.
Among the protesters were separatist leaders Omar Farooq, Abdul Gani Lone, Syed Ali Shah Geelani and Yasim Malik.
Hurriyat head Omar Farooq accused India of sponsoring "state terrorism" in Kashmir.
Kashmiri Samiti general secretary Sunil Shakdher denounced the Hurriyat. "They are the killers and actual violators of human rights of hundreds of thousands of Kashmiri Pandits," he said.

Each camp presented letters to the United Nations office, news agencies said. The Hurriyat asked it to "intervene effectively and ensure that human rights violations by security forces are stopped", the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The Indian government says it has punished security officers who violated Kashmiris' rights.
